title: The Problem of Long-Term Dependencies
summary: The vanishing gradient problem in RNNs creates real implications for tracking long-term dependencies in data. Multiplying many small gradient values together biases the model toward shorter-term dependencies because further back time steps suffer from propagated errors and vanishing gradients.

key_points.text: Vanishing gradients make it difficult for RNNs to track long-term dependencies due to multiplying many small numbers together.
Bias parameters capture short-term dependencies effectively while posing problems for longer input lengths.

concepts.definition: A phenomenon where multiplying many small gradient values together over time steps causes gradients to shrink, making it difficult to learn long-term dependencies.

title: Gating Mechanisms in Neurons
summary: To better control information flow and state updates, internal computations in RNNs can be made more complex using gates. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks introduced a pioneering gated cell to track information across many time steps.

key_points.text: Idea: use gates to selectively add and remove information within each recurrent unit with pointwise multiplication.
Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks rely on a gated cell to track information throughout many time steps.

concepts.definition: A network architecture relying on a gated cell to track information throughout many time steps.
Mechanisms that optionally let information through the cell using pointwise multiplication.

title: RNN Applications & Limitations
summary: Recurrent neural networks can be applied to multi-output generation problems such as music generation, which is explored in software lab 1. An example includes training a recurrent model to finish Franz Schubert's unfinished symphony.

key_points.text: Software lab 1 focuses on multi-output generation problems like music generation.
Recurrent models can be trained on classical music to predict and generate new compositions.

examples: {'text': "Music generation using a recurrent-based model to finish Franz Schubert's unfinished symphony (3rd movement).", 'evidence': 'both'}

title: Limitations of Recurrent Models
summary: Moving beyond recurrent models, the lecture examines the technical limitations of RNNs from a sequence modeling perspective to motivate new architectures.

key_points.text: Evaluate design criteria and capabilities desired with sequence modeling by looking at technical limitations of RNNs.

title: Limitations of Recurrent Models
summary: RNNs suffer from an encoding bottleneck where too much information is compressed into the internal state variable. Processing data step-by-step is slow, lacks parallelization, and struggles with long-term memory.

key_points.text: Encoding bottleneck is imposed by trying to pack structural data into the internal state variable.
Processing time step by time step is slow and not parallelizable.
RNNs quickly run into memory issues regarding how long of a dependency can be captured.

concepts.definition: The limitation imposed by packing all sequence information into a single internal state variable.

title: Goal of Sequence Modeling
summary: Sequence modeling aims to map a sequence of inputs to a sequence of outputs via learned features. RNNs attempt this using recurrence relations and step-by-step modeling.

key_points.text: Goal: take an input sequence and learn features mapping to a sequence of outputs.
RNNs use recurrence relations and step-by-step modeling to track dependencies.

title: Goal of Sequence Modeling
summary: Ideal sequence modeling capabilities eliminate the encoding bottleneck, treat the sequence as a continuous global stream, allow efficient parallelization, and maintain long memory without processing strictly step-by-step.

key_points.text: Desired capabilities include a continuous stream, parallelization, and long memory.
Eliminating recurrence entirely is considered as a potential approach to overcome bottlenecks.

title: Goal of Sequence Modeling: Feed Everything
summary: A naive approach of concatenating all inputs into a single dense network eliminates recurrence but lacks scalability, loses order information, has no temporal dependency, and fails to form long memory.

key_points.text: Idea I: Feed everything into a dense network with no recurrence.
Concatenated inputs are not scalable, lose order, and lack long memory.
The breakthrough idea is to mathematically devise a way for the network to identify and attend to locally and globally important dependencies.

concepts.definition: A mathematical mechanism allowing a network to learn how to pick up and identify locally and globally important dependencies in a sequence.

title: Attention Is All You Need
summary: The attention operation serves as the backbone for transformer architectures like GPT and BERT. It provides an elegant and intuitive mechanism for sequence modeling.

key_points.text: Attention is the foundational mechanism behind transformer architectures like GPT and BERT.

concepts.definition: A neural network architecture whose foundational mechanism is the attention operation.

title: Intuition Behind Self-Attention
summary: Self-attention involves identifying the most important parts of an input and extracting features with high attention scores, functioning similarly to a search problem.

key_points.text: Attending to the most important parts of an input is similar to a search problem.
Step 1 is identifying which parts to attend to, and Step 2 is extracting features with high attention.

title: Simple Example: Search
summary: A search example illustrates how users look up relevant information in a large database, mapping to the concept of querying and retrieving keys.

key_points.text: Searching the internet or YouTube for videos relevant to a query serves as an analogy for attention.

examples: {'text': 'Searching YouTube for videos about neural networks and deep learning.', 'evidence': 'speech'}

title: Understanding Attention with Search
summary: In a database like YouTube, an attention mask computes the semantic similarity between a query (Q) and multiple keys (K) to determine relevance.

key_points.text: Compute an attention mask to see how similar each key is to the desired query.
Find semantic overlap between the search query and the keys (titles) of database entries.

concepts.definition: The search input used to probe the database.
Information representing the indices or titles of items in a database.
A weighting metric measuring how similar each key is to the desired query.

title: Understanding Attention with Search: Values
summary: Once attention scores identify the correct keys, the corresponding values (the actual content or videos) are extracted based on the highest attention scores.

key_points.text: Extract values based on attention by returning the values with the highest attention.

concepts.definition: The actual content or data item that is extracted based on high attention scores.

title: Learning Self-Attention with Neural Networks
summary: Self-attention aims to identify and attend to important features in a sequence fed in all at once, requiring position information to preserve order.

key_points.text: Goal: identify and attend to the most important features in input data fed in all at once.
Need to encode position information to understand order when data is fed in all at once.

examples: {'text': "Input sentence: 'he tossed the tennis ball to serve'", 'evidence': 'speech'}

title: Position-Aware Encoding
summary: Positional embeddings are used to represent inputs in an attention mechanism, mathematically preserving positional relationships in sequence inputs.

key_points.text: Positional embeddings represent the input given into an attention mechanism.
Position-aware encoding preserves information about positional relationships in sequence inputs.

concepts.definition: An encoding used to represent input and preserve information about positional relationships in a sequence.

title: Query, Key, and Value Components
summary: Self-attention applies three transformations to the positional embedding to extract the query, key, and value vectors for assessing internal relationships within a single sequence.

key_points.text: Query, key, and value are the fundamental components of the attention mechanism.
Self-attention extracts core relationships within an individual sequence input using three transformations.

title: Query Matrix Transformation
summary: A learned linear layer transforms the positional embedding into a query matrix.

key_points.text: Query is created by a learned linear layer that transforms the positional embedding into a query matrix.

title: Key and Value Matrix Transformations
summary: Separate learned linear layers transform the identical positional embedding into key and value matrices, capturing different types of information.

key_points.text: Separate learned layers generate the key matrix and the value matrix from the same positional embedding.
The three transformed outputs (query, key, value) capture different information.

title: Attention Score Computation
summary: Attention scores are computed as the pairwise similarity between each query and key using a scaled dot product operation.

key_points.text: Attention score: compute pairwise similarity between each query and key.
Compute how aligned vectors are in space using the dot product between query and key, then scale it.

formulas_or_code: {'formula': 'Q K^T', 'description': 'Dot product between query and key matrices'}

title: Similarity Metric and Cosine Similarity
summary: Applying the dot product and scaling to matrices yields a similarity metric, which is also known as cosine similarity.

key_points.text: Apply dot product and scaling to matrices to get a similarity metric, also known as cosine similarity.

concepts.definition: A similarity metric computed via dot product and scaling between query and key.

title: Attention Weighting and Softmax
summary: Attention scores are processed via scaling and a softmax function to produce attention weights between zero and one, revealing relative importances and semantic relationships within the sequence.

key_points.text: Attention weighting determines how similar the key is to the query and where to attend.
Apply the softmax function to squash values between zero and one to get attention weights.
The attention matrix entries give the relative importance of parts of the input sequence relative to each other.

concepts.definition: A function applied to scaled attention scores to squash values between zero and one.

examples: {'text': "Sequence input: 'he tossed the tennis ball to serve', showing high relation between 'ball' and 'toss'.", 'evidence': 'speech'}

title: Extracting Features with Attention
summary: The final step of self-attention multiplies the attention weights by the value matrix to extract the desired features.

key_points.text: Last step: self-attend to extract features by multiplying attention weighting with the value.

title: Self-Attention Architecture Overview
summary: Architecturally, positional encodings are copied three times and passed through three learned neural network layers to form query, key, and value representations.

key_points.text: Architecturally, sequence positional encoding has three copies fed into three learned neural network layers for query, key, and value.

title: The Attention Head
summary: Combining matrix multiplication of queries and keys, scaling, softmax, and multiplication with values forms a self-attention head that plugs into larger transformer networks.

key_points.text: Operations include MatMul, Scale, Softmax, and MatMul with Query, Key, and Value.
These operations form an attention head that can plug into a larger network architecture, with each head attending to different parts of the input.

concepts.definition: A foundational module combining query-key similarity, scaling, softmax, and value multiplication that can plug into a larger network.

title: Transformer Building Block
summary: Attention serves as the foundational building block of the transformer architecture.

key_points.text: Attention is the foundational building block of the Transformer architecture.

title: Applying Multiple Self-Attention Heads
summary: Multiple attention heads can be stacked together within a single network in a parallelizable manner to learn and identify different patterns of importance.

key_points.text: Attention heads are very parallelizable and can be stacked together within one network to identify different patterns of importance.

examples: {'text': 'Visually picking out Ironman, a building, and an alien spaceship using multiple attention heads.', 'evidence': 'speech'}

title: Self-Attention Applied to Language Processing
summary: Transformers and large language models like GPT have achieved remarkable capabilities in natural language processing.

key_points.text: Transformers and LLMs like GPT have revolutionized natural language processing.

title: Self-Attention Across Domains
summary: Transformer-based architectures are applied across multiple domains, including biological sequences (protein structure models like AlphaFold), natural language processing (GPT), and computer vision (Vision Transformers).

key_points.text: Transformers apply to biological sequences (protein structure models), computer vision (Vision Transformers), and natural language processing (LLMs).

concepts.definition: Transformer models applied to the visual domain for computer vision.

examples: {'text': 'GPT for language, Protein Structure Models (Jumper et al.), Vision Transformers (Dosovitskiy et al.).', 'evidence': 'slide'}

title: Lecture Summary
summary: The lecture covered sequence modeling tasks, RNNs with recurrence and backpropagation through time, applications like music generation, and limitations like the encoding bottleneck that motivated self-attention and large language models.

key_points.text: RNNs are well-suited for sequence modeling and trained via backpropagation through time.
Applications include music generation, classification, and machine translation.
Self-attention models sequences without recurrence and forms the basis for many large language models.
